# Overview

HT1080 RNA-seq from **two batches**, integrated under DESeq2:

| Batch     | Source dir                            | Samples included |
|-----------|---------------------------------------|------------------|
| AUG_2025  | `counts/STAR_v2_PARfix/AUG_2025_HT1080_LOY/`     | 3 CTRL, 3 LOY, 3 PARENTAL |
| MAY_2026  | `counts/STAR_v2_PARfix/MAY_2026_HT1080_ADDBACK/` | 3 sgCTRL, 3 LOY (12 add-back arms excluded) |

Total n = **15 samples**. The MAY_2026 add-back arms (`LOY_LXHA`, `LOY_UTY_AB`,
`LOY_KDM5D_AB`, `LOY_KDM5D_UTY_AB`) live in `analysis/HT1080_ADDBACK/` and
are not part of this report.

**Conventions.**

- `CTRL` and `sgCTRL` from the two batches are merged into a single `CTRL`
  level — both are sgRNA non-targeting controls generated by the same
  protocol.
- `PARENTAL` is **kept in the DESeqDataSet** (size factors, dispersion, PCA)
  but is **excluded from the primary contrast**; the test is strictly
  `LOY − CTRL`.
- Each batch independently went through nucleofection → 3 replicate passages.
  Passages 1/2/3 in batch AUG_2025 are **not** the same biological units as
  passages 1/2/3 in batch MAY_2026; the design uses nested-individual
  encoding (`~ batch + batch:ind.n + treatment`, DESeq2 vignette Section 3.3).
- Every figure is saved to `figures_combined/` as both PNG (review) and PDF
  (publication).

**Primary model.** The conservative primary model for downstream
interpretation is `~ batch + treatment`, because replicate numbers are treated
as independent sample labels rather than true paired/blocking units. The
nested model (`~ batch + batch:ind.n + treatment`) is retained as a sensitivity
analysis.

This is the initial scaffold: load → QC → PCA → DE → volcano. GSEA / TF
activity / chromatin / paralog sections will be added in follow-up Rmds.

***

## 1.2 Paths, parameters, helpers

```{r define-paths}
BASE_DIR    <- getwd()
COUNTS_BASE <- "A:/Dropbox/LOY_paralogs/projects/RNAseq/counts/STAR_v2_PARfix"
COUNTS_DIRS <- list(
  AUG_2025 = file.path(COUNTS_BASE, "AUG_2025_HT1080_LOY"),
  MAY_2026 = file.path(COUNTS_BASE, "MAY_2026_HT1080_ADDBACK")
)
DE_DIR    <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "DE")
GSEA_DIR  <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "GSEA")
ENRICHR_DIR <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "Enrichr")
FIG_DIR   <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "figures_combined")

for (d in c(DE_DIR, GSEA_DIR, ENRICHR_DIR, FIG_DIR)) {
  if (!dir.exists(d)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)
}

ALPHA   <- 0.05
LFC_THR <- 0.75

treatment_cols <- c("CTRL"     = "#009E73",
                    "LOY"      = "#E69F00",
                    "PARENTAL" = "#999999")
batch_shapes   <- c("AUG_2025" = 16, "MAY_2026" = 17)

save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".png")),
         plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf")),
         plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi)
  cat(sprintf("Saved: %s.(png|pdf)  [%gx%g in]\n", name, width, height))
  invisible(plot)
}

safe_fwrite <- function(x, file) {
  tryCatch(
    fwrite(x, file),
    error = function(e) {
      stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))
      ext  <- tools::file_ext(file)
      alt  <- file.path(
        dirname(file),
        sprintf("%s_%s.%s", stem, format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"), ext)
      )
      warning(sprintf(
        "Could not write %s; writing timestamped copy instead: %s",
        file, alt
      ))
      fwrite(x, alt)
    }
  )
}

excel_safe_symbol <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(x), NA_character_, paste0('="', x, '"'))
}
```

## 1.3 Build the sample sheet (both batches)

```{r build-samples}
build_samples_for_batch <- function(batch_name, dir) {
  fs <- list.files(dir, pattern = "^HT1080.*\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
  fs <- fs[!grepl("\\.summary$", fs)]
  base <- sub("\\.txt$", "", basename(fs))

  df <- data.frame(
    sample_id = base,
    file_path = fs,
    batch     = batch_name,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      treatment = case_when(
        # Order matters: most-specific first. Add-back arms are excluded later.
        grepl("-LOY-KDM5D-UTY-AB-", sample_id) ~ "LOY_KDM5D_UTY_AB",
        grepl("-LOY-KDM5D-AB-",     sample_id) ~ "LOY_KDM5D_AB",
        grepl("-LOY-UTY-AB-",       sample_id) ~ "LOY_UTY_AB",
        grepl("-LOY-LXHA-",         sample_id) ~ "LOY_LXHA",
        grepl("-PARENTAL-",         sample_id) ~ "PARENTAL",
        grepl("-LOY-",              sample_id) ~ "LOY",
        grepl("-sgCTRL-",           sample_id) ~ "CTRL",
        grepl("-CTRL-",             sample_id) ~ "CTRL",
        TRUE                                   ~ NA_character_
      ),
      passage = sub(".*-(\\d+)$", "\\1", sample_id)
    )

  # Keep only CTRL / LOY / PARENTAL — drop the four MAY_2026 add-back arms.
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(treatment %in% c("CTRL", "LOY", "PARENTAL"))

  stopifnot(!any(is.na(df$treatment)))
  stopifnot(all(grepl("^\\d+$", df$passage)))
  df
}

samples <- bind_rows(lapply(names(COUNTS_DIRS), function(b)
                            build_samples_for_batch(b, COUNTS_DIRS[[b]])))

# Sample IDs collide between batches (both have HT1080-LOY-1); make column
# names unique by appending the batch tag.
samples$colname <- paste0(samples$sample_id, "__", samples$batch)

samples$treatment <- factor(samples$treatment,
                            levels = c("CTRL", "LOY", "PARENTAL"))
samples$batch     <- factor(samples$batch,
                            levels = c("AUG_2025", "MAY_2026"))
samples$passage   <- factor(samples$passage, levels = c("1", "2", "3"))
# Within-batch individual index — required for the nested DESeq2 design.
samples$ind.n     <- samples$passage
samples$y_status  <- ifelse(samples$treatment == "LOY", "Y-", "Y+")

samples %>%
  group_by(batch, treatment) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            passages = paste(sort(unique(as.character(passage))),
                             collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(
    "Sample summary (n = %d total)", nrow(samples)))
```

## 1.4 Load count matrices + EnsDb annotation

```{r load-counts}
genes <- ensembldb::genes(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86) %>% as.data.frame()

df_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(samples)), function(i) {
  d <- fread(samples$file_path[i], data.table = FALSE, header = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::select(1, 7)
  names(d) <- c("geneID", samples$colname[i])
  column_to_rownames(d, var = "geneID")
})

count_matrix <- do.call("cbind", df_list)
count_matrix <- count_matrix[grepl("^ENSG", rownames(count_matrix)), ]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(count_matrix), samples$colname))

cat(sprintf("Loaded count matrix: %d genes x %d samples\n",
            nrow(count_matrix), ncol(count_matrix)))

# Annotate genes via EnsDb (drop version suffix from Ensembl IDs first)
gene_ids_full  <- rownames(count_matrix)
gene_ids_clean <- gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_ids_full)
gene_info <- genes[match(gene_ids_clean, genes$gene_id), ]
gene_info$gene_id <- ifelse(is.na(gene_info$gene_id),
                            gene_ids_clean, gene_info$gene_id)
rownames(gene_info) <- gene_ids_full

# Keep only genes with a symbol + entrez id (matches the per-batch convention)
keep_anno <- !is.na(gene_info$gene_name) & !is.na(gene_info$entrezid)
count_matrix <- count_matrix[keep_anno, ]
gene_info    <- gene_info[keep_anno, ]
cat(sprintf("After annotation filter: %d genes\n", nrow(count_matrix)))
```

# 2. QC & Normalization

## 2.1 Build DESeqDataSet, filter low counts

```{r build-dds}
rownames(samples) <- samples$colname
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_matrix,
  colData   = samples,
  design    = ~ batch + batch:ind.n + treatment
)

# Pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 reads in at least 3 samples
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3
dds  <- dds[keep, ]
gene_info_kept <- gene_info[keep, ]
cat(sprintf("Genes retained after pre-filter (>=10 in >=3 samples): %d\n",
            nrow(dds)))
```

## 2.2 Size factors & library sizes

```{r size-factors}
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)

tibble(
  sample      = colData(dds)$sample_id,
  batch       = as.character(colData(dds)$batch),
  treatment   = as.character(colData(dds)$treatment),
  passage     = as.character(colData(dds)$passage),
  lib.size_M  = round(colSums(counts(dds)) / 1e6, 1),
  size_factor = round(sizeFactors(dds), 3)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Library sizes & DESeq2 size factors")
```

## 2.3 VST transform

```{r vst}
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("VST: %d genes x %d samples\n", nrow(vsd), ncol(vsd)))
```

## 2.4 PCA — all samples {.tabset}

```{r pca-helpers}
compute_pca <- function(vsd_obj, ngenes = 2000) {
  m <- assay(vsd_obj)
  ngenes <- min(ngenes, nrow(m))
  rv <- matrixStats::rowVars(m)
  ord <- order(rv, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(ngenes)]
  X  <- t(m[ord, , drop = FALSE])
  pca <- prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  npc <- min(5, ncol(pca$x))
  list(
    df = cbind(as.data.frame(colData(vsd_obj)),
               as.data.frame(pca$x[, seq_len(npc), drop = FALSE])) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("row_id"),
    var_exp    = (pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2),
    rotation   = pca$rotation,          # gene loadings (variable genes x PCs)
    genes_used = rownames(m)[ord]       # Ensembl IDs of the top-variance genes
  )
}

plot_pca <- function(pca_obj, x_pc = "PC1", y_pc = "PC2",
                     title, subtitle = NULL) {
  xi <- as.integer(sub("PC", "", x_pc))
  yi <- as.integer(sub("PC", "", y_pc))
  hull_df <- pca_obj$df %>%
    group_by(treatment) %>%
    dplyr::slice(chull(.data[[x_pc]], .data[[y_pc]])) %>%
    ungroup()

  ggplot(pca_obj$df,
         aes(.data[[x_pc]], .data[[y_pc]])) +
    geom_polygon(data = hull_df,
                 aes(x = .data[[x_pc]], y = .data[[y_pc]],
                     fill = treatment, group = treatment),
                 alpha = 0.2, color = NA, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(aes(color = treatment, shape = batch), size = 4) +
    geom_text_repel(aes(label = sample_id),
                    size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf, color = "black") +
    scale_color_manual(values = treatment_cols) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = batch_shapes, name = "Batch") +
    labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = paste0(x_pc, " (",
                 round(pca_obj$var_exp[xi] * 100, 1), "%)"),
      y = paste0(y_pc, " (",
                 round(pca_obj$var_exp[yi] * 100, 1), "%)")
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)
}

pca_all <- compute_pca(vsd)
```

## 2.5 PCA loadings & PC–metadata association

The PCA above is run on the top-2000-variance genes (scaled). Two questions:
(a) **which experimental factor drives each PC** — working hypothesis is
PC1 = batch, PC2 = passage, PC3 = Y-loss (LOY) — and (b) **which genes load
each PC**. The Y-loss axis should be obvious from the loadings: a PC that
separates LOY from CTRL/PARENTAL should be loaded by chrY genes (RPS4Y1,
DDX3Y, EIF1AY, UTY, KDM5D, USP9Y, ZFY, …).

### PC–metadata association (ANOVA R²)

For each PC, the fraction of its sample-score variance explained by each
metadata factor is the one-way ANOVA R² (η²) of `PC ~ factor`. This assigns
a driver to each PC empirically rather than by eye. `Treatment` is the
Y-loss axis (LOY is the only Y− group; CTRL/PARENTAL are Y+).

```{r pca-metadata-association, fig.height=4, fig.width=7.5}
pc_cols      <- paste0("PC", 1:5)
meta_factors <- c(Batch = "batch", Passage = "passage", Treatment = "treatment")

assoc <- expand.grid(PC = pc_cols, Factor = names(meta_factors),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
assoc$R2 <- mapply(function(pc, fac_label) {
  fac <- meta_factors[[fac_label]]
  summary(lm(pca_all$df[[pc]] ~ pca_all$df[[fac]]))$r.squared
}, assoc$PC, assoc$Factor)

assoc$var_exp <- pca_all$var_exp[as.integer(sub("PC", "", assoc$PC))] * 100
assoc$PC_lab  <- factor(sprintf("%s\n(%.1f%%)", assoc$PC, assoc$var_exp),
                        levels = sprintf("%s\n(%.1f%%)", pc_cols,
                                         pca_all$var_exp[1:5] * 100))
assoc$Factor  <- factor(assoc$Factor,
                        levels = rev(c("Batch", "Passage", "Treatment")))

p_assoc <- ggplot(assoc, aes(x = PC_lab, y = Factor, fill = R2)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", R2)), size = 4.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#B2182B", limits = c(0, 1),
                      name = expression(R^2)) +
  labs(title    = "Variance in each PC explained by sample metadata",
       subtitle = "One-way ANOVA R² (η²) per factor · PC label shows overall variance explained",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text  = element_text(color = "black"))
print(p_assoc)
save_fig(p_assoc, "pca_metadata_association_R2", width = 7.5, height = 4)

knitr::kable(
  assoc %>%
    dplyr::select(PC, Factor, R2) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Factor, values_from = R2) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(PC),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "ANOVA R² (η²): fraction of each PC explained by each factor")
```

### Top gene loadings per PC

```{r pca-loadings-tables, results='asis'}
loadings_mat <- pca_all$rotation[, pc_cols, drop = FALSE]
anno_idx     <- match(rownames(loadings_mat), rownames(gene_info_kept))

load_long <- tibble::tibble(
  gene_id_full = rownames(loadings_mat),
  gene_name    = gene_info_kept$gene_name[anno_idx],
  chr          = as.character(gene_info_kept$seqnames[anno_idx])
) %>%
  dplyr::bind_cols(as.data.frame(loadings_mat)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gene_name = ifelse(is.na(gene_name) | !nzchar(gene_name),
                                   gene_id_full, gene_name))

fwrite(load_long, file.path(DE_DIR, "pca_combined_loadings_PC1-5.csv"))

for (pc in pc_cols) {
  tbl <- load_long %>%
    dplyr::mutate(abs_load = abs(.data[[pc]])) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs_load)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(gene_name, chr, loading = round(.data[[pc]], 4))
  n_y <- sum(tbl$chr == "Y")
  cat(sprintf("\n\n**%s** — top 20 genes by |loading| (%d on chrY)\n\n", pc, n_y))
  print(knitr::kable(tbl, row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n")
}
```

### Loadings plot (top 15 per PC)

chrY genes highlighted — the PC whose top loadings are chrY is the Y-loss axis.

```{r pca-loadings-plot, fig.height=6, fig.width=16}
load_plot_one <- function(pc) {
  d <- load_long %>%
    dplyr::mutate(abs_load = abs(.data[[pc]])) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs_load)) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 15) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(lbl  = factor(make.unique(gene_name),
                                levels = rev(make.unique(gene_name))),
                  is_Y = ifelse(chr == "Y", "chrY", "other"))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[pc]], y = lbl, fill = is_Y)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("chrY" = "#2166AC", "other" = "grey65"),
                      name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = pc, x = "loading", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.title  = element_text(face = "bold"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, color = "black"))
}

p_loadings <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  lapply(pc_cols, load_plot_one), nrow = 1, guides = "collect") +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Top gene loadings, PC1–PC5 (combined batches)",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)))
print(p_loadings)
save_fig(p_loadings, "pca_loadings_PC1-5", width = 16, height = 6)
```

## 2.6 Batch-corrected PCA {.tabset}

`limma::removeBatchEffect()` applied to the VST matrix, with `design =
model.matrix(~ treatment)` preserving the treatment signal while regressing
out the batch main effect. This is a **visualization-only** correction —
the DE in Section 3 still uses the full DESeq2 model with `batch` as a covariate
(no batch effect is removed from the count-level data).

The corrected matrix collapses the AUG_2025 vs MAY_2026 separation that
shows up on PC2 above; remaining variance should reflect treatment +
within-batch biology.

```{r vsd-batch-correct}
vsd_bc <- vsd
treatment_design <- model.matrix(~ treatment, data = colData(vsd_bc))
assay(vsd_bc) <- limma::removeBatchEffect(
  assay(vsd_bc),
  batch  = colData(vsd_bc)$batch,
  design = treatment_design
)

pca_bc <- compute_pca(vsd_bc)
```

### PC1 vs PC2 (batch-corrected)

```{r pca-bc-pc12, fig.height=6, fig.width=8}
p_bc_12 <- plot_pca(
  pca_bc, "PC1", "PC2",
  title    = "HT1080 — PCA after limma::removeBatchEffect",
  subtitle = "Color = treatment; shape = batch (residual batch separation should be minimal)"
)
print(p_bc_12)
save_fig(p_bc_12, "pca_batchcorrected_pc1_pc2", width = 8, height = 6)
```

### PC1 vs PC3 (batch-corrected)

```{r pca-bc-pc13, fig.height=6, fig.width=8}
p_bc_13 <- plot_pca(
  pca_bc, "PC1", "PC3",
  title    = "HT1080 — PCA after batch correction, PC1 vs PC3",
  subtitle = "Color = treatment; shape = batch"
)
print(p_bc_13)
save_fig(p_bc_13, "pca_batchcorrected_pc1_pc3", width = 8, height = 6)
```

### Variance explained — before vs after

```{r bc-varexp, fig.height=4, fig.width=7}
ve_compare <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(PC = paste0("PC", 1:5),
             variance_pct = pca_all$var_exp[1:5] * 100,
             stage = "Uncorrected"),
  data.frame(PC = paste0("PC", 1:5),
             variance_pct = pca_bc$var_exp[1:5] * 100,
             stage = "Batch-corrected")
) %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = c("Uncorrected", "Batch-corrected")))

p_ve <- ggplot(ve_compare,
               aes(x = PC, y = variance_pct, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
           color = "black", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", variance_pct)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Uncorrected"     = "#4E79A7",
                               "Batch-corrected" = "#F28E2B"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Variance explained per PC",
       y = "Variance explained (%)",
       x = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(p_ve)
save_fig(p_ve, "pca_variance_explained_before_after_bc",
         width = 7, height = 4)
```

## 2.7 Sample distance heatmap

```{r sample-distance, fig.height=9, fig.width=10}
# Unique, informative labels — sample_id alone collides between batches
sd_labels <- paste(colData(vsd)$treatment,
                   colData(vsd)$batch,
                   colData(vsd)$passage, sep = "-")
sample_dist <- as.matrix(dist(t(assay(vsd))))
rownames(sample_dist) <- sd_labels
colnames(sample_dist) <- sd_labels

ann_col <- data.frame(
  Treatment = colData(vsd)$treatment,
  Batch     = colData(vsd)$batch,
  Passage   = as.character(colData(vsd)$passage),
  row.names = colnames(sample_dist)
)
ann_colors <- list(
  Treatment = treatment_cols,
  Batch     = c("AUG_2025" = "#4E79A7", "MAY_2026" = "#F28E2B"),
  Passage   = c("1" = "#CCCCCC", "2" = "#888888", "3" = "#444444")
)

pal <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, "Blues")))(255)

# Wrap the pheatmap call once; drawing target is the current graphics device.
# png()/pdf() open a new device on top of knitr's, so calls inside go to file;
# the final call (no device wrap) goes to knitr's device → one inline render.
draw_sample_dist <- function() {
  pheatmap(sample_dist,
           color = pal,
           annotation_col = ann_col,
           annotation_colors = ann_colors,
           show_rownames = TRUE, show_colnames = TRUE,
           fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 8,
           main = "HT1080 combined batches — Sample distance matrix")
}

png(file.path(FIG_DIR, "sample_distance_matrix.png"),
    width = 10, height = 9, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
draw_sample_dist(); dev.off()

pdf(file.path(FIG_DIR, "sample_distance_matrix.pdf"),
    width = 10, height = 9)
draw_sample_dist(); dev.off()

# Inline
draw_sample_dist()
```

## 2.8 Sample distance heatmap — ComBat-corrected counts

`sva::ComBat_seq()` adjusts the raw count matrix for batch effects (negative
binomial-aware, returns integer counts). The corrected counts are re-VST'd
and the sample distance matrix recomputed. Should show LOY samples
clustering across batches (vs the uncorrected version where AUG_2025 and
MAY_2026 may form sub-clusters within treatment groups).

```{r combat-sample-distance, fig.height=9, fig.width=10}
# ComBat_seq on raw counts, preserving the treatment design
counts_combat <- sva::ComBat_seq(
  counts    = counts(dds),
  batch     = as.character(colData(dds)$batch),
  group     = as.character(colData(dds)$treatment)
)

# Build a temporary DESeqDataSet on the corrected counts and VST-transform
dds_combat <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts_combat,
  colData   = colData(dds),
  design    = ~ treatment
)
dds_combat <- estimateSizeFactors(dds_combat)
vsd_combat <- vst(dds_combat, blind = FALSE)

# Sample distance matrix
sd_labels_cb <- paste(colData(vsd_combat)$treatment,
                      colData(vsd_combat)$batch,
                      colData(vsd_combat)$passage, sep = "-")
sample_dist_cb <- as.matrix(dist(t(assay(vsd_combat))))
rownames(sample_dist_cb) <- sd_labels_cb
colnames(sample_dist_cb) <- sd_labels_cb

ann_col_cb <- data.frame(
  Treatment = colData(vsd_combat)$treatment,
  Batch     = colData(vsd_combat)$batch,
  Passage   = as.character(colData(vsd_combat)$passage),
  row.names = colnames(sample_dist_cb)
)

draw_sample_dist_cb <- function() {
  pheatmap(sample_dist_cb,
           color = pal,
           annotation_col = ann_col_cb,
           annotation_colors = ann_colors,
           show_rownames = TRUE, show_colnames = TRUE,
           fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 8,
           main = "HT1080 — Sample distance (ComBat_seq-corrected counts)")
}

png(file.path(FIG_DIR, "sample_distance_matrix_combat.png"),
    width = 10, height = 9, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
draw_sample_dist_cb(); dev.off()

pdf(file.path(FIG_DIR, "sample_distance_matrix_combat.pdf"),
    width = 10, height = 9)
draw_sample_dist_cb(); dev.off()

draw_sample_dist_cb()
```

## 2.9 Y chromosome QC

Confirm that LOY samples (regardless of batch) show markedly lower Y-gene
expression than CTRL/PARENTAL.

```{r y-chromosome, fig.height=13, fig.width=20}
chrY_info <- genes %>%
  dplyr::filter(seqnames == "Y", gene_biotype == "protein_coding") %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_name, start) %>%
  arrange(start)

vsd_mat <- assay(vsd)
sym_for_vsd <- gene_info_kept$gene_name[
  match(rownames(vsd_mat), rownames(gene_info_kept))]
# Collapse symbol duplicates by max variance
rv <- matrixStats::rowVars(vsd_mat)
ord <- order(rv, decreasing = TRUE)
vsd_mat_s <- vsd_mat[ord, ]
sym_for_vsd <- sym_for_vsd[ord]
keep_sym <- !duplicated(sym_for_vsd) & !is.na(sym_for_vsd) & nzchar(sym_for_vsd)
vsd_mat_s <- vsd_mat_s[keep_sym, ]
rownames(vsd_mat_s) <- sym_for_vsd[keep_sym]

y_present <- intersect(chrY_info$gene_name, rownames(vsd_mat_s))
y_mat <- vsd_mat_s[y_present, , drop = FALSE]
y_mat <- y_mat[match(chrY_info$gene_name[chrY_info$gene_name %in% y_present],
                     rownames(y_mat)), , drop = FALSE]

cat(sprintf("Y-chr protein-coding genes in VST matrix: %d / %d\n",
            length(y_present), length(chrY_info$gene_name)))

clean_labels <- paste0(colData(vsd)$treatment, "-",
                       colData(vsd)$batch, "-",
                       colData(vsd)$passage)
colnames(y_mat) <- clean_labels

raw_counts <- counts(dds)
lib_sizes <- colSums(raw_counts)
logcpm_mat <- log2(t(t(raw_counts) / lib_sizes * 1e6) + 1)
sym_for_logcpm <- gene_info_kept$gene_name[
  match(rownames(logcpm_mat), rownames(gene_info_kept))]
logcpm_rv <- matrixStats::rowVars(logcpm_mat)
logcpm_ord <- order(logcpm_rv, decreasing = TRUE)
logcpm_mat_s <- logcpm_mat[logcpm_ord, ]
sym_for_logcpm <- sym_for_logcpm[logcpm_ord]
keep_logcpm_sym <- !duplicated(sym_for_logcpm) &
  !is.na(sym_for_logcpm) & nzchar(sym_for_logcpm)
logcpm_mat_s <- logcpm_mat_s[keep_logcpm_sym, ]
rownames(logcpm_mat_s) <- sym_for_logcpm[keep_logcpm_sym]

# Row z-scores make the blue-white-red scale interpretable as relative
# down/up expression per Y-chromosome gene.

y_mat_z[is.na(y_mat_z)] <- 0

)

ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
```

# 3. Differential expression: LOY vs CTRL

DESeq2 model: `~ batch + batch:ind.n + treatment`. The `batch:ind.n` term
absorbs per-batch passage drift. PARENTAL samples contribute to size factors
and dispersion estimation but the primary contrast is strictly `LOY − CTRL`.

## 3.1 Fit

```{r de-fit}
dds <- DESeq(dds)
cat("Result names:\n")
print(resultsNames(dds))
```

## 3.2 LOY vs CTRL results

```{r de-results}
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("treatment", "LOY", "CTRL"),
               alpha = ALPHA)

cat("\nSummary (DESeq2 default):\n")
summary(res)

# GRCh38 PAR coordinates (Ensembl / GENCODE convention)
PAR1_Y_END    <- 2781479L      # PAR1: chrY 10,001 - 2,781,479
PAR2_Y_START  <- 56887903L     # PAR2: chrY 56,887,903 - 57,217,415
Y_CENTRO_MID  <- 10500000L     # rough centromere midpoint (between 10.32-10.54 Mb)
PAR1_X_END    <- 2781479L
PAR2_X_START  <- 155701383L
PAR1_SYMBOLS <- c("PLCXD1", "GTPBP6", "PPP2R3B", "SHOX", "CRLF2",
                  "CSF2RA", "IL3RA", "SLC25A6", "ASMTL", "P2RY8",
                  "AKAP17A", "ASMT", "DHRSX", "ZBED1", "CD99", "XG")
PAR2_SYMBOLS <- c("SPRY3", "VAMP7", "IL9R")

classify_y_region <- function(chr, start, symbol = NA_character_) {
  case_when(
    symbol %in% PAR1_SYMBOLS            ~ "PAR1",
    symbol %in% PAR2_SYMBOLS            ~ "PAR2",
    chr == "X" & start <= PAR1_X_END    ~ "PAR1",
    chr == "X" & start >= PAR2_X_START  ~ "PAR2",
    chr == "Y" & start <= PAR1_Y_END    ~ "PAR1",
    chr == "Y" & start >= PAR2_Y_START  ~ "PAR2",
    is.na(chr) | chr != "Y"             ~ "Other",
    start < Y_CENTRO_MID                ~ "Yp_MSY",
    TRUE                                ~ "Yq_MSY"
  )
}

annotate_deseq_result <- function(res_obj) {
  res_df <- as.data.frame(res_obj)
  if (!"stat" %in% names(res_df)) {
    res_df$stat <- NA_real_
  }
  res_df %>%
    rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
    mutate(gene_id = gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id_full)) %>%
    left_join(
      gene_info_kept %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
        mutate(entrezid_chr = vapply(entrezid, function(x) {
          if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[[1]])) NA_character_
          else as.character(x[[1]])
        }, character(1))) %>%
        dplyr::select(gene_id_full, gene_name,
                      entrezid = entrezid_chr,
                      chr = seqnames, gene_start = start, gene_end = end,
                      biotype = gene_biotype),
      by = "gene_id_full"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      logFC  = log2FoldChange,
      PValue = pvalue,
      FDR    = padj,
      logCPM = baseMean,
      t      = stat
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      chr_region = classify_y_region(chr, gene_start, gene_name),
      gene_name_excel_safe = excel_safe_symbol(gene_name)
    ) %>%
    arrange(PValue)
}

de_loy_ctrl <- as.data.frame(res) %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
  mutate(gene_id = gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id_full)) %>%
  left_join(
    gene_info_kept %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
      mutate(entrezid_chr = vapply(entrezid, function(x) {
        if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[[1]])) NA_character_
        else as.character(x[[1]])
      }, character(1))) %>%
      dplyr::select(gene_id_full, gene_name,
                    entrezid = entrezid_chr,
                    chr = seqnames, gene_start = start, gene_end = end,
                    biotype = gene_biotype),
    by = "gene_id_full"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    logFC  = log2FoldChange,
    PValue = pvalue,
    FDR    = padj,
    logCPM = baseMean,
    t      = stat
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    chr_region = classify_y_region(chr, gene_start, gene_name),
    gene_name_excel_safe = excel_safe_symbol(gene_name)
  ) %>%
  arrange(PValue)

cat("\nY/PAR gene counts by region (in DE table):\n")
de_loy_ctrl %>%
  dplyr::filter(chr_region != "Other") %>%
  dplyr::count(chr_region) %>%
  knitr::kable()

cat(sprintf("\nTested genes:                       %d\n", nrow(de_loy_ctrl)))
cat(sprintf("FDR < %g:                          %d\n",
            ALPHA, sum(de_loy_ctrl$FDR < ALPHA, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("FDR < %g & |logFC| > %g:           %d (up: %d, down: %d)\n",
            ALPHA, LFC_THR,
            sum(de_loy_ctrl$FDR < ALPHA &
                  abs(de_loy_ctrl$logFC) > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(de_loy_ctrl$FDR < ALPHA &
                  de_loy_ctrl$logFC >  LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(de_loy_ctrl$FDR < ALPHA &
                  de_loy_ctrl$logFC < -LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE)))

fwrite(de_loy_ctrl,
       file.path(DE_DIR, "ht1080_batches_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2.csv"))
```

## 3.3 Volcano (publication style)

```{r make-volcano}
make_volcano <- function(de, title, fdr_thr = ALPHA,
                         lfc_thr = LFC_THR, n_label = 50,
                         up_label = "Up", down_label = "Down",
                         xlab = expression(log[2]~"Fold Change")) {
  up_lvl   <- up_label
  down_lvl <- down_label
  d <- de %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(PValue), !is.na(FDR), !is.na(logFC)) %>%
    mutate(
      nlp = -log10(pmax(PValue, 1e-300)),
      sig = FDR < fdr_thr & abs(logFC) >= lfc_thr,
      direction = case_when(
        sig & logFC >  lfc_thr ~ up_lvl,
        sig & logFC < -lfc_thr ~ down_lvl,
        TRUE                   ~ "NS"
      ),
      direction = factor(direction, levels = c(down_lvl, "NS", up_lvl))
    )
  n_up   <- sum(d$direction == up_lvl)
  n_down <- sum(d$direction == down_lvl)
  top    <- d %>% dplyr::filter(sig) %>% slice_min(PValue, n = n_label)
  cols   <- setNames(c("#0072B2", "grey80", "#D55E00"),
                     c(down_lvl, "NS", up_lvl))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = logFC, y = nlp)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = direction), alpha = 0.7, size = 1.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc_thr, lfc_thr), linetype = "dashed",
               color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text_repel(
      data = top, aes(label = gene_name),
      size = 3, fontface = "italic",
      max.overlaps = Inf, segment.color = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3,
      box.padding = 0.4, point.padding = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0.2,
      force = 2
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cols, drop = FALSE) +
    annotate("text",
             x = max(d$logFC, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.85,
             y = max(d$nlp,   na.rm = TRUE) * 0.95,
             label = paste0("n = ", n_up),
             color = "#D55E00", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    annotate("text",
             x = min(d$logFC, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.85,
             y = max(d$nlp,   na.rm = TRUE) * 0.95,
             label = paste0("n = ", n_down),
             color = "#0072B2", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
    labs(
      x = xlab,
      y = expression(-log[10]~"(P-value)"),
      title = title,
      color = NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.text     = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title      = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      axis.text       = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
      plot.title      = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 13)
    )
}
```

```{r volcano-plot, fig.height=7, fig.width=8}
p_vol <- make_volcano(
  de_loy_ctrl,
  title      = "HT1080 combined batches: LOY vs CTRL (DESeq2)",
  up_label   = "Up in LOY",
  down_label = "Down in LOY",
  xlab       = expression(log[2]~"Fold Change (LOY / CTRL)")
)
print(p_vol)
save_fig(p_vol, "volcano_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2", width = 8, height = 7)
```

## 3.4 Volcano with Y/PAR regions highlighted

Y/PAR genes split into four functional regions:
**PAR1** (pseudoautosomal, Yp tip, also on Xp) ·
**PAR2** (pseudoautosomal, Yq tip, also on Xq) ·
**Yp_MSY** (male-specific Y, short arm) ·
**Yq_MSY** (male-specific Y, long arm).
GRCh38 PAR coordinates: PAR1 chrY 10,001–2,781,479; PAR2 chrY
56,887,903–57,217,415; centromere ~10.5 Mb.

EnsDb annotates many PAR genes on chrX, so PAR classification uses both
coordinates and known PAR gene symbols.

```{r volcano-y-region, fig.height=8.5, fig.width=10}
y_cols <- c(
  "Other"   = "grey85",
  "PAR1"    = "#1B7837",   # green
  "PAR2"    = "#762A83",   # purple
  "Yp_MSY"  = "#D6604D",   # red/orange
  "Yq_MSY"  = "#2166AC"    # blue
)

vol_df <- de_loy_ctrl %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(PValue), !is.na(logFC)) %>%
  mutate(
    nlp = -log10(pmax(PValue, 1e-300)),
    chr_region = factor(chr_region,
                        levels = c("Other", "PAR1", "PAR2",
                                   "Yp_MSY", "Yq_MSY"))
  )

# Label significant Y/PAR genes.
y_to_label <- vol_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(chr_region != "Other",
                FDR < ALPHA & abs(logFC) > LFC_THR) %>%
  slice_min(PValue, n = 30)

# Region count annotation (Y/PAR genes only)
region_counts <- vol_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(chr_region != "Other") %>%
  dplyr::count(chr_region) %>%
  arrange(chr_region)
counts_caption <- paste(
  sprintf("%s: %d", region_counts$chr_region, region_counts$n),
  collapse = " · ")

p_vol_y <- ggplot(vol_df, aes(x = logFC, y = nlp)) +
  # Plot non-Y genes underneath
  geom_point(data = ~dplyr::filter(., chr_region == "Other"),
             color = "grey85", alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  # Plot Y-region genes on top, larger
  geom_point(data = ~dplyr::filter(., chr_region != "Other"),
             aes(color = chr_region), alpha = 0.9, size = 2.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-LFC_THR, LFC_THR), linetype = "dashed",
             color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = y_to_label, aes(label = gene_name, color = chr_region),
    size = 3.2, fontface = "italic",
    max.overlaps = Inf, segment.color = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3,
    box.padding = 0.4, point.padding = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0.2,
    force = 2, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = y_cols, drop = FALSE,
                     name = "Y/PAR region") +
  labs(
    x = expression(log[2]~"Fold Change (LOY / CTRL)"),
    y = expression(-log[10]~"(P-value)"),
    title = "HT1080: LOY vs CTRL - Y/PAR genes highlighted",
    subtitle = paste("Y/PAR genes in DE table -", counts_caption)
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title      = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text       = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
    plot.title      = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "grey30")
  )
print(p_vol_y)
save_fig(p_vol_y, "volcano_LOY_v_CTRL_Y_regions",
         width = 10, height = 8.5)
```

## 3.5 Volcano excluding MSY (male-specific Y) genes

The male-specific Y (MSY = chrY minus PAR1/PAR2) contains the Y-specific
gene set that mechanically disappears with LOY and dominates the volcano.
Removing MSY genes lets the autosomal + PAR transcriptional response
become visible. PAR1/PAR2 genes are retained.

```{r volcano-no-msy, fig.height=7, fig.width=8}
n_msy <- sum(de_loy_ctrl$chr_region %in% c("Yp_MSY", "Yq_MSY"), na.rm = TRUE)
n_par <- sum(de_loy_ctrl$chr_region %in% c("PAR1", "PAR2"),    na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Removed %d MSY genes (Yp + Yq) from the volcano.\n", n_msy))
cat(sprintf("Retained %d PAR1/PAR2 genes.\n", n_par))

de_no_msy <- de_loy_ctrl %>%
```

## 3.7 Sensitivity analysis: batch + treatment design

This fit drops the nested passage/blocking term and uses the simpler design
`~ batch + treatment`. This is the appropriate sensitivity check if replicate
numbers are independent sample labels rather than true within-batch paired
units.

```{r de-batch-treatment}
dds_batch_treatment <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts(dds),
  colData   = colData(dds),
  design    = ~ batch + treatment
)

dds_batch_treatment <- DESeq(dds_batch_treatment)
res_batch_treatment <- results(
  dds_batch_treatment,
  contrast = c("treatment", "LOY", "CTRL"),
  alpha = ALPHA
)

cat("\nSummary for design ~ batch + treatment:\n")
summary(res_batch_treatment)

de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment <- as.data.frame(res_batch_treatment) %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
  mutate(gene_id = gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id_full)) %>%
  left_join(
    gene_info_kept %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
      mutate(entrezid_chr = vapply(entrezid, function(x) {
        if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[[1]])) NA_character_
        else as.character(x[[1]])
      }, character(1))) %>%
      dplyr::select(gene_id_full, gene_name,
                    entrezid = entrezid_chr,
                    chr = seqnames, gene_start = start, gene_end = end,
                    biotype = gene_biotype),
    by = "gene_id_full"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    logFC  = log2FoldChange,
    PValue = pvalue,
    FDR    = padj,
    logCPM = baseMean,
    t      = stat
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    chr_region = classify_y_region(chr, gene_start, gene_name),
    gene_name_excel_safe = excel_safe_symbol(gene_name)
  ) %>%
  arrange(PValue)

fwrite(
  de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment,
  file.path(DE_DIR, "ht1080_batches_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2_batch_treatment.csv")
)

summarise_de <- function(de, model) {
  tibble(
    model = model,
    tested = nrow(de),
    fdr_0.05 = sum(de$FDR < ALPHA, na.rm = TRUE),
    fdr_0.05_lfc_0.75 = sum(de$FDR < ALPHA &
                              abs(de$logFC) > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE),
    up = sum(de$FDR < ALPHA & de$logFC > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE),
    down = sum(de$FDR < ALPHA & de$logFC < -LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

de_model_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarise_de(de_loy_ctrl, "~ batch + batch:ind.n + treatment"),
  summarise_de(de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment, "~ batch + treatment")
)

knitr::kable(
  de_model_summary,
  caption = "LOY vs CTRL DE summary by model"
)

sig_nested <- de_loy_ctrl %>%
  dplyr::filter(FDR < ALPHA, abs(logFC) > LFC_THR) %>%
  dplyr::pull(gene_id_full)
sig_batch_treatment <- de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment %>%
  dplyr::filter(FDR < ALPHA, abs(logFC) > LFC_THR) %>%
  dplyr::pull(gene_id_full)

cat(sprintf(
  "\nSignificant DEG overlap at FDR<%g and |logFC|>%g: %d / %d nested, %d batch+treatment\n",
  ALPHA, LFC_THR,
  length(intersect(sig_nested, sig_batch_treatment)),
  length(sig_nested),
  length(sig_batch_treatment)
))

model_compare <- de_loy_ctrl %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_id_full, gene_name, logFC_nested = logFC,
                FDR_nested = FDR) %>%
  inner_join(
    de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment %>%
      dplyr::select(gene_id_full, logFC_batch_treatment = logFC,
                    FDR_batch_treatment = FDR),
    by = "gene_id_full"
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "logFC Pearson correlation between models: %.4f\n",
  cor(model_compare$logFC_nested,
      model_compare$logFC_batch_treatment,
      use = "complete.obs")
))
```

```{r volcano-batch-treatment-netrin, fig.height=7, fig.width=8.5}
      sig & logFC < -LFC_THR ~ "Down in LOY",
```

```{r volcano-batch-treatment-no-msy-treat, fig.height=7, fig.width=8}
res_batch_treatment_treat <- results(
  dds_batch_treatment,
  contrast = c("treatment", "LOY", "CTRL"),
  lfcThreshold = LFC_THR,
  altHypothesis = "greaterAbs",
  alpha = ALPHA
)

      mutate(entrezid_chr = vapply(entrezid, function(x) {
        if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x[[1]])) NA_character_
        else as.character(x[[1]])
      }, character(1))) %>%
      dplyr::select(gene_id_full, gene_name,
                    entrezid = entrezid_chr,
                    chr = seqnames, gene_start = start, gene_end = end,
                    biotype = gene_biotype),
    by = "gene_id_full"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    logFC  = log2FoldChange,
    PValue = pvalue,
    FDR    = padj,
    logCPM = baseMean,
    t      = stat
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    chr_region = classify_y_region(chr, gene_start, gene_name),
    gene_name_excel_safe = excel_safe_symbol(gene_name)
  ) %>%
  arrange(PValue)

fwrite(
  de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment_treat,
  file.path(DE_DIR,
            "ht1080_batches_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2_batch_treatment_treat_lfc0.75.csv")
)
```

## 3.9 LFC shrinkage sensitivity

`apeglm` shrinkage is used for visualization/ranking sensitivity on the
primary `~ batch + treatment` model. Formal DE calls above remain based on the
unshrunken DESeq2 Wald statistics.

```{r lfc-shrinkage, fig.height=7, fig.width=8}
coef_name <- "treatment_LOY_vs_CTRL"
if (coef_name %in% resultsNames(dds_batch_treatment)) {
  res_batch_treatment_shrunk <- lfcShrink(
    dds_batch_treatment,
    coef = coef_name,
    type = "apeglm"
  )
  de_batch_treatment_shrunk <- annotate_deseq_result(
    res_batch_treatment_shrunk
  )
  de_batch_treatment_shrunk_no_msy <- de_batch_treatment_shrunk %>%
    dplyr::filter(!chr_region %in% c("Yp_MSY", "Yq_MSY"))

  safe_fwrite(
    de_batch_treatment_shrunk_no_msy,
    file.path(DE_DIR,
              "ht1080_batches_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2_batch_treatment_apeglm_no_MSY.csv")
  )

  p_vol_shrunk <- make_volcano(
    de_batch_treatment_shrunk_no_msy,
    title      = "HT1080: LOY vs CTRL (~ batch + treatment) - apeglm, MSY excluded",
    up_label   = "Up in LOY",
    down_label = "Down in LOY",
    xlab       = expression(shrunken~log[2]~"Fold Change (LOY / CTRL)")
  )
  print(p_vol_shrunk)
  save_fig(p_vol_shrunk, "volcano_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2_batch_treatment_apeglm_no_MSY",
           width = 8, height = 7)
} else {
  cat("Could not find coefficient for lfcShrink. Available coefficients:\n")
  print(resultsNames(dds_batch_treatment))
}
```

## 3.10 Batch-stratified LOY effects

Each batch is fit separately with `~ treatment` using CTRL and LOY samples only.
This checks whether the combined LOY effect is shared across AUG_2025 and
MAY_2026 rather than being driven by one batch.

```{r batch-stratified-de, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
run_batch_de <- function(batch_name) {
  keep_cols <- colData(dds)$batch == batch_name &
    colData(dds)$treatment %in% c("CTRL", "LOY")
  cd <- as.data.frame(colData(dds)[keep_cols, ])
  cd$treatment <- droplevels(factor(cd$treatment, levels = c("CTRL", "LOY")))
  cd$batch <- droplevels(cd$batch)
  dds_b <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
    countData = counts(dds)[, keep_cols],
    colData   = cd,
    design    = ~ treatment
  )
  dds_b <- DESeq(dds_b)
  annotate_deseq_result(
    results(dds_b, contrast = c("treatment", "LOY", "CTRL"),
            alpha = ALPHA)
  ) %>%
    mutate(batch_fit = batch_name)
}

de_batch_aug <- run_batch_de("AUG_2025")
de_batch_may <- run_batch_de("MAY_2026")

safe_fwrite(de_batch_aug,
            file.path(DE_DIR, "ht1080_AUG_2025_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2.csv"))
safe_fwrite(de_batch_may,
            file.path(DE_DIR, "ht1080_MAY_2026_LOY_v_CTRL_DESeq2.csv"))

batch_lfc_compare <- de_batch_aug %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_id_full, gene_name,
                logFC_AUG_2025 = logFC, FDR_AUG_2025 = FDR) %>%
  inner_join(
    de_batch_may %>%
      dplyr::select(gene_id_full, logFC_MAY_2026 = logFC,
                    FDR_MAY_2026 = FDR),
    by = "gene_id_full"
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    de_batch_treatment_no_msy %>%
      dplyr::select(gene_id_full, chr_region),
    by = "gene_id_full"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!chr_region %in% c("Yp_MSY", "Yq_MSY"))

cat(sprintf(
  "Batch-stratified logFC Pearson correlation: %.3f\n",
  cor(batch_lfc_compare$logFC_AUG_2025,
      batch_lfc_compare$logFC_MAY_2026,
      use = "complete.obs")
))

p_batch_lfc <- ggplot(batch_lfc_compare,
                      aes(x = logFC_AUG_2025, y = logFC_MAY_2026)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(color = "grey70", alpha = 0.45, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "AUG_2025 log2FC (LOY / CTRL)",
    y = "MAY_2026 log2FC (LOY / CTRL)",
    title = "Batch-stratified LOY effect concordance"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
print(p_batch_lfc)
save_fig(p_batch_lfc, "batch_stratified_logFC_concordance_no_MSY",
         width = 6, height = 6)
```

## 3.11 Treatment-by-batch interaction

This model uses CTRL and LOY samples only and tests whether the LOY effect is
different in MAY_2026 relative to AUG_2025.

```{r treatment-batch-interaction}
keep_lc <- colData(dds)$treatment %in% c("CTRL", "LOY")
cd_int <- as.data.frame(colData(dds)[keep_lc, ])
cd_int$treatment <- droplevels(factor(cd_int$treatment,
                                      levels = c("CTRL", "LOY")))
cd_int$batch <- droplevels(cd_int$batch)
dds_interaction <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts(dds)[, keep_lc],
  colData   = cd_int,
  design    = ~ batch + treatment + batch:treatment
)
dds_interaction <- DESeq(dds_interaction)
cat("Interaction model coefficients:\n")
print(resultsNames(dds_interaction))

int_coef <- grep("batch.*MAY.*treatment.*LOY|treatment.*LOY.*batch.*MAY",
                 resultsNames(dds_interaction), value = TRUE)
if (length(int_coef) == 1) {
  res_interaction <- results(dds_interaction, name = int_coef, alpha = ALPHA)
  de_interaction <- annotate_deseq_result(res_interaction)
  de_interaction_no_msy <- de_interaction %>%
    dplyr::filter(!chr_region %in% c("Yp_MSY", "Yq_MSY"))
  safe_fwrite(
    de_interaction_no_msy,
    file.path(DE_DIR,
              "ht1080_batches_treatment_by_batch_interaction_no_MSY.csv")
  )

  cat(sprintf(
    "Interaction genes FDR<%g: %d; FDR<%g & |logFC|>%g: %d\n",
    ALPHA, sum(de_interaction_no_msy$FDR < ALPHA, na.rm = TRUE),
    ALPHA, LFC_THR,
    sum(de_interaction_no_msy$FDR < ALPHA &
          abs(de_interaction_no_msy$logFC) > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))

  de_interaction_no_msy %>%
    dplyr::filter(FDR < ALPHA) %>%
    slice_min(FDR, n = 20) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene_name, chr, logFC, PValue, FDR, logCPM) %>%
    knitr::kable(
      digits = c(0, 0, 2, 4, 4, 2),
      caption = "Top treatment-by-batch interaction genes")
} else {
  cat("Could not uniquely identify interaction coefficient.\n")
}
```

## 3.12 GSEA: batch + treatment TREAT-like, MSY excluded

GSEA uses the TREAT-like, MSY-excluded result from section 3.7. Ranks are the
DESeq2 thresholded Wald statistic (`t`) from the `lfcThreshold = 0.75` test,
so pathway enrichment reflects genes that move beyond the selected effect-size
threshold. MSY genes are removed before ranking; PAR genes are retained.

```{r gsea-treat-no-msy-setup}
prep_ranks_t <- function(de_results, gene_col = "gene_name") {
  de_results %>%
    transmute(gene = .data[[gene_col]], stat = t) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(gene), is.finite(stat)) %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarize(stat = stat[which.max(abs(stat))], .groups = "drop") %>%
    { setNames(.$stat, .$gene) } %>%
    sort(decreasing = TRUE)
}

run_fgsea_all <- function(ranks, pathways_list, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500) {
  results <- lapply(names(pathways_list), function(name) {
    cat(sprintf("  Running %s (%d gene sets)...\n", name,
                length(pathways_list[[name]])))
    suppressWarnings(
      fgsea(pathways_list[[name]], ranks,
            minSize = minSize, maxSize = maxSize)
    ) %>%
      mutate(collection = name) %>%
      arrange(padj)
  })
  bind_rows(results)
}

cat("Loading expanded MSigDB collections...\n")
collections <- list(
  hallmark     = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H"),
  reactome     = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C2",
                         subcategory = "CP:REACTOME"),
  kegg         = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C2",
                         subcategory = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY"),

                         subcategory = "CP:BIOCARTA"),

                         subcategory = "CP:PID"),
  wikipathways = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C2",
                         subcategory = "CP:WIKIPATHWAYS"),
  cgp          = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C2",
                         subcategory = "CGP"),

                         subcategory = "GO:BP")
)

for (name in names(pathways)) {

}
```

## 3.14 GSEA regular vs TREAT-like comparison

GSEA uses all ranked genes, while Enrichr below uses thresholded significant
gene lists. This comparison checks whether the pathway-level conclusions are
stable across the regular and TREAT-like DESeq2 rankings.

```{r gsea-regular-treat-compare, fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
gsea_compare <- gsea_regular_no_msy %>%
  dplyr::filter(collection == "hallmark") %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES_regular = NES, padj_regular = padj) %>%
  inner_join(
    gsea_treat_no_msy %>%
      dplyr::filter(collection == "hallmark") %>%
      dplyr::select(pathway, NES_treat = NES, padj_treat = padj),
    by = "pathway"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sig_regular = padj_regular < 0.05,
    sig_treat = padj_treat < 0.05,
    pathway_clean = gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway),
    pathway_clean = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", pathway_clean))
  )

cat(sprintf(
  "Hallmark NES Pearson correlation, regular vs TREAT-like: %.3f\n",
  cor(gsea_compare$NES_regular, gsea_compare$NES_treat,
      use = "complete.obs")
))

gsea_compare %>%
  arrange(padj_regular) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway_clean, NES_regular, padj_regular,
                NES_treat, padj_treat) %>%
  head(15) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(0, 2, 4, 2, 4),
    caption = "Top Hallmark GSEA terms: regular vs TREAT-like rankings")

p_gsea_compare <- ggplot(gsea_compare,
                         aes(x = NES_regular, y = NES_treat)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(color = sig_regular | sig_treat), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = dplyr::filter(gsea_compare, sig_regular | sig_treat),
    aes(label = pathway_clean),
    size = 2.7, max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey65", "TRUE" = "#D55E00"),
                     name = "Significant in either") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "Regular DESeq2 NES",
    y = "TREAT-like NES",
    title = "Hallmark GSEA concordance"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(p_gsea_compare)
save_fig(p_gsea_compare, "gsea_hallmark_regular_vs_treat_NES",
         width = 6, height = 5)
```

## 3.15 Enrichr: significant up/down genes

Enrichr is run on significant no-MSY genes from both `~ batch + treatment`
DESeq2 analyses:

- **regular**: FDR < 0.05 and `|logFC| > 0.75`
- **TREAT-like**: thresholded DESeq2 test with FDR < 0.05 and direction from
  `logFC`

PAR genes are retained.

```{r enrichr-up-down-setup}
enrichr_dbs_requested <- c(
  "MSigDB_Hallmark_2020",
  "KEGG_2021_Human",
  "Reactome_2022",
  "GO_Biological_Process_2023"
)

available_enrichr_dbs <- enrichR::listEnrichrDbs()
enrichr_dbs <- intersect(enrichr_dbs_requested, available_enrichr_dbs$libraryName)
missing_enrichr_dbs <- setdiff(enrichr_dbs_requested, enrichr_dbs)

if (length(missing_enrichr_dbs) > 0) {
  cat("Requested Enrichr libraries not available:\n")
  print(missing_enrichr_dbs)
}
stopifnot(length(enrichr_dbs) > 0)

get_sig_genes <- function(de, direction = c("up", "down")) {
  direction <- match.arg(direction)
  de %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      FDR < ALPHA,
      if (direction == "up") logFC > LFC_THR else logFC < -LFC_THR,
      !is.na(gene_name),
      nzchar(gene_name)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::pull(gene_name) %>%
    unique()
}

enrichr_gene_sets <- list(
  regular_up = get_sig_genes(de_batch_treatment_no_msy, "up"),
  regular_down = get_sig_genes(de_batch_treatment_no_msy, "down"),
  treat_up = get_sig_genes(de_batch_treatment_treat_no_msy, "up"),
  treat_down = get_sig_genes(de_batch_treatment_treat_no_msy, "down")
)

tibble(
  gene_set = names(enrichr_gene_sets),
  n_genes = lengths(enrichr_gene_sets)
) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gene lists submitted to Enrichr")
```

```{r enrichr-up-down-run}
run_enrichr_one <- function(genes, set_name, dbs) {
  if (length(genes) < 5) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  cat(sprintf("Running Enrichr for %s (%d genes)...\n", set_name, length(genes)))
  enr <- enrichR::enrichr(genes, dbs)
  bind_rows(lapply(names(enr), function(db) {
    as_tibble(enr[[db]]) %>%
      mutate(database = db, gene_set = set_name, .before = 1)
  }))
}

enrichr_results <- bind_rows(lapply(names(enrichr_gene_sets), function(nm) {
  run_enrichr_one(enrichr_gene_sets[[nm]], nm, enrichr_dbs)
}))

safe_fwrite(
  enrichr_results,
  file.path(ENRICHR_DIR,
            "ht1080_batches_batch_treatment_no_MSY_regular_and_treat_enrichr.csv")
)

enrichr_results %>%
  group_by(gene_set, database) %>%
  summarize(
    terms = n(),
    sig_terms = sum(Adjusted.P.value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Enrichr significant terms by gene list and database")
```

```{r enrichr-up-down-dotplot, fig.height=9, fig.width=9}
enrichr_top <- enrichr_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(Adjusted.P.value < 0.05) %>%
  group_by(gene_set) %>%
  slice_min(Adjusted.P.value, n = 10) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Term_clean = gsub("\\s*\\([^\\)]*\\)$", "", Term),
    Term_clean = str_wrap(Term_clean, 42),
    gene_set = factor(gene_set,
                      levels = c("regular_up", "regular_down",
                                 "treat_up", "treat_down")),
    term_label = fct_reorder(Term_clean, -log10(Adjusted.P.value))
  )

if (nrow(enrichr_top) > 0) {
  p_enrichr <- ggplot(
    enrichr_top,
    aes(x = -log10(Adjusted.P.value), y = term_label,
        size = Combined.Score, fill = database)
  ) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, color = "black", stroke = 0.25, alpha = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ gene_set, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 5), name = "Combined score") +
    labs(
      x = expression(-log[10]~"(adjusted P-value)"),
      y = NULL,
      title = "HT1080 batches: Enrichr on significant no-MSY genes",
      fill = "Database"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
  print(p_enrichr)
  save_fig(p_enrichr, "enrichr_regular_treat_up_down_no_MSY",
           width = 9, height = 9)
} else {
  cat("No Enrichr terms with adjusted P < 0.05\n")
}
```

## 3.16 DESeq2 QC diagnostics (~ batch + treatment)

Standard DESeq2 diagnostics on the primary `~ batch + treatment` model:
MA plot, dispersion fit, raw p-value histogram (calibration sanity), and
per-sample Cook's distance (outlier check).

### Raw p-value histogram

```{r qc-pval-hist, fig.height=4, fig.width=5.5}
p_pval_hist <- ggplot(
  de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(PValue)),
  aes(x = PValue)
) +
  geom_histogram(boundary = 0, binwidth = 0.02,
                 fill = "#4E79A7", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "DESeq2 raw p-value histogram (~ batch + treatment)",
       x = "Raw p-value", y = "Gene count") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(p_pval_hist)
save_fig(p_pval_hist, "qc_pvalue_histogram_batch_treatment",
         width = 5.5, height = 4)
```

### MA plot

```{r qc-ma, fig.height=5, fig.width=6.5}
draw_ma <- function() {
  DESeq2::plotMA(res_batch_treatment, alpha = ALPHA,
                 main = "MA plot - LOY vs CTRL (~ batch + treatment)",
                 ylim = c(-6, 6))
}
png(file.path(FIG_DIR, "qc_MA_batch_treatment.png"),
    width = 6.5, height = 5, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")

draw_ma()
```

### Cook's distance per sample

```{r qc-cooks, fig.height=5, fig.width=9}
cooks_mat <- assays(dds_batch_treatment)[["cooks"]]
cooks_df <- as.data.frame(cooks_mat) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_id_full") %>%
  pivot_longer(-gene_id_full, names_to = "colname",
               values_to = "cooks") %>%
  left_join(
    samples %>% dplyr::select(colname, sample_id, treatment, batch),
    by = "colname"
  ) %>%
  mutate(label = paste(sample_id, batch, sep = " | "))

p_cooks <- ggplot(cooks_df,
                  aes(x = label, y = log10(cooks + 1e-8),
                      fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6, outlier.alpha = 0.45) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_cols) +
  labs(title = "Cook's distance per sample (~ batch + treatment)",
       x = NULL,
       y = expression(log[10]~"(Cook's distance)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8))
print(p_cooks)
save_fig(p_cooks, "qc_cooks_distance_batch_treatment",
         width = 9, height = 5)

n_samp    <- ncol(dds_batch_treatment)
n_param   <- length(resultsNames(dds_batch_treatment))
cooks_thr <- qf(0.99, n_param, n_samp - n_param)
flag_per_sample <- colSums(cooks_mat > cooks_thr, na.rm = TRUE)
tibble(
  colname       = names(flag_per_sample),
  flagged_genes = flag_per_sample
) %>%
  left_join(
    samples %>% dplyr::select(colname, sample_id, treatment, batch),
    by = "colname"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(flagged_genes)) %>%
  dplyr::select(sample_id, treatment, batch, flagged_genes) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = sprintf(
      "Cook's outlier counts per sample (threshold F(0.99, %d, %d) = %.2f)",
      n_param, n_samp - n_param, cooks_thr
    )
  )
```

## 3.17 Top-50 DEG heatmap (no MSY)

Row-Z-scored VST expression for the top 50 non-MSY DEGs by FDR from the
`~ batch + treatment` result. MSY genes are dropped because they collapse
to zero in LOY samples and would dominate the colour scale; PAR genes are
retained.

```{r top-deg-heatmap, fig.height=11, fig.width=11}
top_n_deg <- 50
top_deg_table <- de_batch_treatment_no_msy %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(FDR), FDR < ALPHA, abs(logFC) > LFC_THR,
                gene_name %in% rownames(vsd_mat_s)) %>%
  slice_min(FDR, n = top_n_deg, with_ties = FALSE)

deg_mat <- vsd_mat_s[top_deg_table$gene_name, , drop = FALSE]
deg_z   <- t(scale(t(deg_mat)))
deg_z[is.na(deg_z)] <- 0
colnames(deg_z) <- paste(colData(vsd)$treatment,
                         colData(vsd)$batch,
                         colData(vsd)$passage, sep = "-")

ha_deg <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Treatment = colData(vsd)$treatment,
  Batch     = colData(vsd)$batch,
  Passage   = as.character(colData(vsd)$passage),
  col = list(Treatment = treatment_cols,
             Batch     = ann_colors$Batch,
             Passage   = ann_colors$Passage),
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 9),
  simple_anno_size = unit(4, "mm")
)

ht_deg <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(
  deg_z,
  name = "row Z",
  col  = z_col_fun,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  clustering_method_rows    = "ward.D2",
  clustering_method_columns = "ward.D2",
  top_annotation = ha_deg,
  row_names_gp    = gpar(fontsize = 9),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  column_names_rot = 60,
  column_title = sprintf(
    "Top %d DEGs by FDR (no MSY, ~ batch + treatment)", nrow(deg_z)),
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 13, fontface = "bold"),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(at = c(-2, 0, 2),
                              labels = c("Down", "Mean", "Up"),
                              legend_height = unit(4, "cm"))
)

draw_top_deg <- function() {
  draw(ht_deg, merge_legend = TRUE,
       padding = unit(c(8, 8, 8, 8), "mm"))
}
png(file.path(FIG_DIR, "top_DEG_heatmap_batch_treatment_no_MSY.png"),
    width = 11, height = 11, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
draw_top_deg(); dev.off()
pdf(file.path(FIG_DIR, "top_DEG_heatmap_batch_treatment_no_MSY.pdf"),
    width = 11, height = 11)
draw_top_deg(); dev.off()
draw_top_deg()
```

## 3.18 Top-50 DEG heatmap (limma batch-corrected VST)

Same top 50 DEGs as Section 3.17, but expression values are pulled from the
`limma::removeBatchEffect`-corrected VST matrix (`vsd_bc`, Section 2.6). The
batch main effect has been regressed out while the treatment design is
preserved, so CTRL samples from AUG_2025 and MAY_2026 should cluster
together more tightly than in the uncorrected version.

```{r top-deg-heatmap-bc, fig.height=11, fig.width=11}
vsd_bc_mat <- assay(vsd_bc)
sym_for_bc <- gene_info_kept$gene_name[
  match(rownames(vsd_bc_mat), rownames(gene_info_kept))]
rv_bc  <- matrixStats::rowVars(vsd_bc_mat)
ord_bc <- order(rv_bc, decreasing = TRUE)
vsd_bc_mat_s <- vsd_bc_mat[ord_bc, ]
sym_for_bc   <- sym_for_bc[ord_bc]
keep_bc_sym  <- !duplicated(sym_for_bc) & !is.na(sym_for_bc) & nzchar(sym_for_bc)
vsd_bc_mat_s <- vsd_bc_mat_s[keep_bc_sym, ]
rownames(vsd_bc_mat_s) <- sym_for_bc[keep_bc_sym]

top_deg_bc <- top_deg_table %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene_name %in% rownames(vsd_bc_mat_s))

deg_mat_bc <- vsd_bc_mat_s[top_deg_bc$gene_name, , drop = FALSE]
deg_z_bc   <- t(scale(t(deg_mat_bc)))
deg_z_bc[is.na(deg_z_bc)] <- 0
colnames(deg_z_bc) <- paste(colData(vsd_bc)$treatment,
                            colData(vsd_bc)$batch,
                            colData(vsd_bc)$passage, sep = "-")

ht_deg_bc <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(
  deg_z_bc,
  name = "row Z",
  col  = z_col_fun,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  clustering_method_rows    = "ward.D2",
  clustering_method_columns = "ward.D2",
  top_annotation = ha_deg,
  row_names_gp    = gpar(fontsize = 9),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
  column_names_rot = 60,
  column_title = sprintf(
    "Top %d DEGs (limma batch-corrected VST, no MSY)", nrow(deg_z_bc)),
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 13, fontface = "bold"),
  heatmap_legend_param = list(at = c(-2, 0, 2),
                              labels = c("Down", "Mean", "Up"),
                              legend_height = unit(4, "cm"))
)

draw_top_deg_bc <- function() {
  draw(ht_deg_bc, merge_legend = TRUE,
       padding = unit(c(8, 8, 8, 8), "mm"))
}
png(file.path(FIG_DIR,
              "top_DEG_heatmap_batch_treatment_no_MSY_batchcorrected.png"),
    width = 11, height = 11, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
draw_top_deg_bc(); dev.off()
pdf(file.path(FIG_DIR,
              "top_DEG_heatmap_batch_treatment_no_MSY_batchcorrected.pdf"),
    width = 11, height = 11)
draw_top_deg_bc(); dev.off()
draw_top_deg_bc()
```

# 4. X-Y paralog deep-dive

LOY removes Y-linked paralogs of broadly expressed X-linked dosage genes
(KDM6A/UTY, KDM5C/KDM5D, DDX3X/DDX3Y, etc.). The biological question is
whether the corresponding X paralog upregulates to compensate for the
lost Y dosage.

## 4.1 Paralog list

```{r xy-paralog-list}
xy_paralogs <- tribble(
  ~X_gene,    ~Y_gene,
  "KDM6A",    "UTY",
  "KDM5C",    "KDM5D",
  "DDX3X",    "DDX3Y",
  "EIF1AX",   "EIF1AY",
  "ZFX",      "ZFY",
  "USP9X",    "USP9Y",
  "RPS4X",    "RPS4Y1",
  "NLGN4X",   "NLGN4Y",
  "TBL1X",    "TBL1Y",
  "TMSB4X",   "TMSB4Y",
  "PRKX",     "PRKY",
  "AMELX",    "AMELY",
  "TXLNG",    "TXLNGY",
  "PCDH11X",  "PCDH11Y",
  "TGIF2LX",  "TGIF2LY"
)

xy_long <- xy_paralogs %>%
  mutate(pair_id    = row_number(),
         pair_label = paste0(X_gene, "/", Y_gene)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(X_gene, Y_gene),
               names_to = "side", values_to = "gene_name") %>%
  mutate(chr_side = recode(side, X_gene = "X", Y_gene = "Y"))

xy_present <- xy_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene_name %in% rownames(vsd_mat_s))

cat(sprintf("Paralog genes present in VST matrix: %d / %d\n",
            nrow(xy_present), nrow(xy_long)))
missing_xy <- setdiff(xy_long$gene_name, xy_present$gene_name)
if (length(missing_xy) > 0) {
  cat("Missing from VST matrix:\n")
  print(missing_xy)
}
```

## 4.2 Per-sample expression boxplots

```{r xy-paralog-boxplots, fig.height=14, fig.width=14}
vst_long <- as.data.frame(vsd_mat_s) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("gene_name") %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene_name %in% xy_present$gene_name) %>%
  pivot_longer(-gene_name, names_to = "colname", values_to = "vst") %>%
  left_join(
    samples %>% dplyr::select(colname, sample_id, treatment, batch),
    by = "colname"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    xy_long %>% dplyr::select(gene_name, pair_id, pair_label, chr_side),
    by = "gene_name"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pair_id, chr_side) %>%
  mutate(facet_label = paste0(pair_label, "  (", chr_side, ": ",
                              gene_name, ")"),
         facet_label = factor(facet_label, levels = unique(facet_label)))

p_paralog_box <- ggplot(vst_long,
                        aes(x = treatment, y = vst, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.55, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(aes(shape = batch), width = 0.12, size = 1.6,
              color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ facet_label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = batch_shapes, name = "Batch") +
  labs(title = "X-Y paralog VST expression by treatment",
       x = NULL, y = "VST-normalized expression") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"))

print(p_paralog_box)
save_fig(p_paralog_box, "xy_paralog_boxplots",
         width = 14, height = 14)
```

## 4.3 Paralog DE table

```{r xy-paralog-de-table}
de_paralog <- de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene_name %in% xy_long$gene_name) %>%
  left_join(
    xy_long %>% dplyr::select(gene_name, pair_id, pair_label, chr_side),
    by = "gene_name"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pair_id, chr_side) %>%
  dplyr::select(pair_label, chr_side, gene_name, chr,
                logFC, FDR, logCPM)

de_paralog %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 4, 2),
    caption = "LOY vs CTRL DE statistics for X-Y paralog pairs (~ batch + treatment)")
```

## 4.4 Paired X vs Y log2FC

For each pair, the Y bar should be strongly negative (Y dosage loss); a
positive X bar in the same pair would be evidence of paralog-specific
compensation.

```{r xy-paralog-paired-lfc, fig.height=6, fig.width=10}
de_paralog_bars <- de_paralog %>%
  mutate(sig = !is.na(FDR) & FDR < ALPHA & abs(logFC) > LFC_THR)

y_lfc_per_pair <- de_paralog_bars %>%
  dplyr::filter(chr_side == "Y") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pair_label) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(logFC_y = mean(logFC, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

pair_levels <- y_lfc_per_pair %>%
  arrange(logFC_y) %>%
  dplyr::pull(pair_label)
pair_levels <- c(pair_levels,
                 setdiff(unique(de_paralog_bars$pair_label), pair_levels))

de_paralog_bars <- de_paralog_bars %>%
  mutate(pair_label = factor(pair_label, levels = pair_levels))

p_paired_lfc <- ggplot(de_paralog_bars,
                       aes(x = pair_label, y = logFC,
                           fill = chr_side, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), color = "black",
           linewidth = 0.3, width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-LFC_THR, LFC_THR),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.35) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("X" = "#762A83", "Y" = "#1B7837"),
                    name = "Chromosome") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 0.95, "FALSE" = 0.45),
                     guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "X-Y paralog log2FC (LOY / CTRL)",
       subtitle = "Faded = FDR>=0.05 or |logFC|<0.75",
       x = NULL, y = "log2FC (LOY / CTRL)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

print(p_paired_lfc)
save_fig(p_paired_lfc, "xy_paralog_paired_logFC",
         width = 10, height = 6)
```

# 5. chrX compensation

Does the chrX transcriptome shift upward in LOY samples to compensate
for lost Y dosage? Tested by comparing the chrX (non-PAR) log2FC
distribution against the autosomal background. A positive median shift
in X vs autosomes is the canonical compensation signal.

## 5.1 Setup

```{r chrx-comp-setup}
chr_logfc <- de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(logFC), !is.na(chr)) %>%
  mutate(
    chr_group = case_when(
      chr_region == "PAR1"                              ~ "PAR1",
      chr_region == "PAR2"                              ~ "PAR2",
      chr_region %in% c("Yp_MSY", "Yq_MSY")             ~ "Y (MSY)",
      chr == "X"                                        ~ "X (non-PAR)",
      chr %in% as.character(1:22)                       ~ "Autosome",
      TRUE                                              ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(chr_group != "Other") %>%
  mutate(chr_group = factor(chr_group,
                            levels = c("Autosome", "X (non-PAR)",
                                       "PAR1", "PAR2", "Y (MSY)")))

chr_cols <- c("Autosome"    = "grey60",
              "X (non-PAR)" = "#762A83",
              "PAR1"        = "#1B7837",
              "PAR2"        = "#5AAE61",
              "Y (MSY)"     = "#B2182B")
```

## 5.2 log2FC density and violin

```{r chrx-density, fig.height=4.5, fig.width=8}
p_chr_density <- ggplot(chr_logfc,
                        aes(x = logFC, fill = chr_group,
                            color = chr_group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.55) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = chr_cols, name = "Region") +
  scale_color_manual(values = chr_cols, name = "Region") +
  labs(title = "log2FC density by chromosomal region",
       subtitle = "Positive X (non-PAR) shift vs autosomes = X compensation",
       x = "log2FC (LOY / CTRL)", y = "Density") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(p_chr_density)
save_fig(p_chr_density, "chrX_compensation_density",
         width = 8, height = 4.5)
```

```{r chrx-violin, fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
p_chr_violin <- ggplot(chr_logfc,
                       aes(x = chr_group, y = logFC, fill = chr_group)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.55, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, fill = "white",
               outlier.size = 0.3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = chr_cols, guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-4, 4)) +
  labs(title = "log2FC by chromosomal region",
       x = NULL, y = "log2FC (LOY / CTRL)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
print(p_chr_violin)
save_fig(p_chr_violin, "chrX_compensation_violin",
         width = 7, height = 5)
```

## 5.3 Summary statistics and Wilcoxon tests

```{r chrx-stats}
chr_summary <- chr_logfc %>%
  group_by(chr_group) %>%
  summarize(
    n            = n(),
    median_logFC = median(logFC, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_logFC   = mean(logFC,   na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_up       = 100 * mean(logFC > 0,        na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_up_sig   = 100 * mean(logFC > LFC_THR &
                              FDR  < ALPHA,     na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
chr_summary %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 1, 2),
               caption = "log2FC summary by chromosomal region")

x_lfc    <- chr_logfc$logFC[chr_logfc$chr_group == "X (non-PAR)"]
auto_lfc <- chr_logfc$logFC[chr_logfc$chr_group == "Autosome"]
w_one <- wilcox.test(x_lfc, auto_lfc, alternative = "greater")
w_two <- wilcox.test(x_lfc, auto_lfc, alternative = "two.sided")

cat(sprintf("Wilcoxon (one-sided, X > Autosome): p = %.3g\n", w_one$p.value))
cat(sprintf("Wilcoxon (two-sided)              : p = %.3g\n", w_two$p.value))
cat(sprintf(
  "Median X (non-PAR) logFC = %.3f; median autosome logFC = %.3f; shift = %.3f\n",
  median(x_lfc, na.rm = TRUE),
  median(auto_lfc, na.rm = TRUE),
  median(x_lfc, na.rm = TRUE) - median(auto_lfc, na.rm = TRUE)
))
```

## 5.4 chrX expression vs log2FC (MA-style)

```{r chrx-ma, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=8.5}
chrx_de <- de_loy_ctrl_batch_treatment %>%
  dplyr::filter(chr == "X",
                !is.na(logFC), !is.na(FDR), !is.na(logCPM)) %>%
  mutate(sig_label = case_when(
    FDR < ALPHA & logFC >  LFC_THR ~ "Up in LOY",
    FDR < ALPHA & logFC < -LFC_THR ~ "Down in LOY",
    TRUE                            ~ "NS"
  ),
  sig_label = factor(sig_label,
                     levels = c("Down in LOY", "NS", "Up in LOY")))

top_x_label <- chrx_de %>%
  dplyr::filter(FDR < ALPHA, abs(logFC) > LFC_THR) %>%
  slice_min(FDR, n = 25)

p_chrx_ma <- ggplot(chrx_de, aes(x = log2(logCPM + 1), y = logFC)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-LFC_THR, LFC_THR),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_point(aes(color = sig_label), alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = top_x_label, aes(label = gene_name),
                  size = 2.9, fontface = "italic",
                  max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0.2,
                  segment.color = "grey55", segment.size = 0.3,
                  box.padding = 0.35) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Up in LOY"   = "#D55E00",
                                 "Down in LOY" = "#0072B2",
                                 "NS"          = "grey75"),
                     name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "chrX genes: log2FC vs expression (LOY vs CTRL)",
       x = expression(log[2]*"(baseMean + 1)"),
       y = "log2FC (LOY / CTRL)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)
print(p_chrx_ma)
save_fig(p_chrx_ma, "chrX_MA_plot",
         width = 8.5, height = 5.5)
```

# 6. Biological summary

The primary downstream model is `~ batch + treatment`; the nested model is kept
as sensitivity. MSY genes are excluded from pathway-focused interpretation
because their loss is a direct consequence of LOY and can dominate volcano axes
and ranked lists. PAR genes are retained and explicitly classified even when
EnsDb represents them on chrX.

```{r biological-summary}
summary_counts <- tibble(
  analysis = c("regular no-MSY", "TREAT-like no-MSY"),
  significant = c(nrow(sig_de_regular_no_msy), nrow(sig_de_treat_no_msy)),
  up = c(sum(sig_de_regular_no_msy$logFC > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE),
         sum(sig_de_treat_no_msy$logFC > LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE)),
  down = c(sum(sig_de_regular_no_msy$logFC < -LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE),
           sum(sig_de_treat_no_msy$logFC < -LFC_THR, na.rm = TRUE))
)
summary_counts %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Primary batch+treatment no-MSY DE summary")

netrin_summary <- de_batch_treatment_no_msy %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene_name %in% netrin_genes) %>%
  arrange(PValue) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_name, logFC, FDR)
netrin_summary %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(0, 2, 4),
    caption = "Netrin pathway genes in primary no-MSY DE result")

hallmark_summary <- gsea_regular_no_msy %>%
  dplyr::filter(collection == "hallmark", padj < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(padj) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES, padj)
hallmark_summary %>%
  mutate(pathway = gsub("^HALLMARK_", "", pathway),
         pathway = str_to_title(gsub("_", " ", pathway))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(0, 2, 4),
    caption = "Significant Hallmark pathways in regular no-MSY GSEA")
```

**Interpretation.** Y/MSY expression loss is confirmed across batches. After
removing MSY genes, the non-MSY transcriptional response is still broad. The
most consistent biological signals are up-regulation of neuronal/axon-guidance
and netrin-related genes, including strong `UNC5A` and `NTN1` induction, and
down-regulation of inflammatory/interferon, angiogenesis, EMT, and ECM-related
programs. The TREAT-like analysis is more conservative at the gene level but
retains the same qualitative pathway direction for the dominant Hallmark
signals.
